subject: Re: Skyline Payments — temporary log retention & segmentation request
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@skylinepayments.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@skylinepayments.com>, security@skylinepayments.com
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary extended retention for fraud investigation

Hi Rishi,

Quick note from Skyline Security — we're in the middle of a multi-merchant fraud investigation and need to keep a narrowly scoped set of debug traces and transaction-level debug logs longer than your standard window. Specifically: payment_transactions, chargeback-trace events, and dispute-enrichment debug logs for three merchant IDs (I attached a short list).

Ask: can Redwood retain those classes for 180 days (instead of the default ephemeral window) and restrict access to only Skyline-designated engineers? We also need SIG/CAIQ evidence around log segmentation, KMS usage, and audit trail exports to satisfy our internal audit.

We're happy to sign any temporary amendment or MAP. Can you let us know:
- Whether Redwood can materially do selective retention by log-tag/tenant,
- What artifacts you can provide for SIG/CAIQ to show controls,
- Estimated cost for 180-day retention and timeline to enable.

Thanks — attaching the investigation brief and a CSV with the merchant IDs.

Aaron Lee
Head of Risk Ops | Skyline Payments
Attachments: investigation-brief.pdf, merchant-list.csv

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extended retention for fraud investigation

Aaron — thanks for the context and the attachments. Looping in Kimberly (security) and Marissa (CS) to scope and operationalize. Short answers up front:

- Selective retention by tenant and log tag is possible; we have an implementation path that can persist tagged traces for a limited window.
- We can produce SIG/CAIQ excerpts and a SOC-2 oriented artifact package (audit logs, KMS key rotation records, access control lists) — Kimberly can list the exact items.
- Timeline: we can get an initial show-of-capability in ~5 business days; enabling full retention for production traffic will likely be 7–10 business days after sign-off.

Practical next steps:
1) Kimberly to confirm the specific artifacts we can provide and any sampling constraints.
2) Marissa to get engagement/PO/legal sign-off for a short-term MAP/amendment.
3) I’ll provide a ballpark cost for a 180-day retention delta after we confirm scope.

Can you confirm the merchant IDs and whether Skyline requires logs to be exported to your storage or retained within Redwood with restricted access?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0148
Attachment: template-MAP.docx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extended retention for fraud investigation — artifacts & controls

Aaron / team — I reviewed the ask with the infra and compliance teams. Below is a concise assessment and what we can/should provide.

Architecture / feasibility:
- Redwood stores ephemeral debug traces in a short-lived shard (default 30 days). We support tenant-level tags and named retention policies that can persist a subset of logs to a hardened, access-controlled bucket.
- Implementation options: (A) Keep the tagged traces in Redwood with RBAC + audit logging, or (B) export an encrypted snapshot to your S3-compatible endpoint on a rolling cadence.

Security artifacts we can provide (examples):
- SOC 2: audit trail excerpts showing admin/engineer access to the retention policy change event(s).
- SIG: control excerpts for LOG-01 (log collection), LOG-02 (retention), CRYPTO-01 (KMS usage) — we will provide a redacted CAIQ mapping.
- Sample audit logs: user action events, IP geolocation, and a timestamped KMS key usage entry for the period when the retention policy is applied.

Compensating controls we recommend during the hold:
- Limit access to a named Skyline role (we can create a Skyline-specific IAM role).
- Enable read-only export token if you prefer copies outside Redwood.
- Enable weekly delivery of an access-audit snapshot (CSV) for Skyline auditors.

Work effort & timeline:
- Quick proof-of-capability (non-prod sample with 2–3 records): 2 business days.
- Production enablement (policy, IAM role, audit sampling, documentation): 5–7 business days.

Constraints / compliance notes:
- We cannot alter transactions themselves; only debug/trace retention.
- For SIG/CAIQ, we provide control excerpts and sampled artifacts; full raw audit exports are restricted for security reasons but can be provided under a controlled escrow process if requested by legal.

I'll attach the segmentation implementation playbook and a SOC2 checklist for the requested artifacts.

—Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Red Team
Redwood Inference
Attachments: segmentation-implementation-playbook.pdf, soc2-log-collection.md

From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@skylinepayments.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Priya Nair <priya.nair@skylinepayments.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skyline Payments — temporary log retention & segmentation request

Thanks Kimberly / Rishi — that sounds workable. To be explicit:
- Scope: payment_transactions, chargeback_trace, dispute_enrichment_debug for merchant IDs: 1193, 2231, 8874 (merchant-list.csv attached).
- We prefer Redwood to hold the logs (option A) under a Skyline-specific role, rather than exporting snapshots, for ease of access during investigation.
- We'll need: SOC2 audit excerpts for the policy-change event, CAIQ mapping for LOG & CRYPTO controls, and a weekly access-audit CSV.

One more ask: do you have an estimate for incremental storage and operational cost for 180-day retention of the scoped classes (ballpark for budgeting). Also confirm whether Redwood will require a DPA amendment or a temporary addendum.

Aaron
Attachments: merchant-list.csv

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2027 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Skyline Payments — temporary log retention & segmentation request — MAP & estimate

Aaron — thanks, this is clear. Summary / MAP below (for signature):

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Scope: persist debug traces labeled: payment_transactions, chargeback_trace, dispute_enrichment_debug for merchant IDs 1193, 2231, 8874.
- Retention window: 180 days from ingestion; auto-expire thereafter.
- Access: Skyline-specific IAM role + RBAC; Redwood engineers only for emergencies (requires approval).
- Artifacts: SOC2 audit excerpt (policy-change event), CAIQ mapping for LOG/CRYPTO, weekly access-audit CSV (sampled fields).
- Export: Not required; Redwood will host. Option to export on request.

Estimated cost (ballpark):
- Incremental storage & retention delta: $420/month (covers storage + reduced compression for trace format).
- Operational setup: one-time $1,250 (policy config, IAM role creation, audit snapshot pipeline).

Pre-reqs:
1) Signed MAP or DPA amendment (legal).
2) PO/charge code for monthly/one-time fees.

Timeline:
- Legal sign-off and PO: dependent on Skyline (we can proceed with a provisional hold on a non-production sample without paperwork).
- Production enablement after sign-off: 5 business days.

I've created a DocuSign draft for the MAP (link below). Please have your legal/ops teams review and sign; once signed we'll schedule the enablement slot.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/sig-amendment
Hub ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1234

I'll attach the MAP template and the sig/soc2 artifacts bundle we referenced.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachment: sig-and-soc2-artifacts.zip

Priya Nair
